A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sum-of-Parts research, with matching authors, method, theoretical results, and experiments. Their text, figures, tables, and appendices A-D support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original ImageNet-S, CosmoGrid, and MultiRC experiments, human evaluation, probing studies, and cosmological analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and reports additional baseline comparisons, a group-count ablation, and revised human-evaluation results.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the attention-based group generator, binary masks, frozen backbone, sparse group selector, and scaled training losses. Algorithm 1 is relocated and notation standardized without establishing a changed SOP procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet/ImageNet-S classification, CosmoGrid parameter regression, and MultiRC reading comprehension. The enlarged human study and group-count ablation remain within existing task and population coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds FastShap-F, ViT-Shapley-F, and AutoGnothi-F comparisons on ImageNet-S in Appendix C.6 and Table A9. Table 1 also adds an explicit backbone comparator row. The original fourteen comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: Appendix C.4.6 expands the reported human-study sample from 10 images/classes to 100, retaining three judgments per image. v4 also introduces controls using 1, 2, 5, 10, and 20 groups. CosmoGrid's feature-preparation description replaces the earlier patch/watershed account with CNN-grid details; this documents revised settings without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 adds an ablation testing performance against group count. v4 removes the separate correct/incorrect group-purity analysis and preliminary patch/quickshift/watershed comparison, while retaining object-reliance debugging, sparsity tests, purity-threshold ablations, and perturbation robustness checks.

E5.justification: Both versions report human-study standard deviations using 1,000 bootstrap resamples and retain the existing uncertainty displays for matched benchmark results. The larger human sample changes evaluation design, not the stated uncertainty-estimation procedure; no new seed or repeated-run protocol is documented.

E6.justification: The human-evaluation evidence is substantially revised under the enlarged sample: SOP is among the higher means in v3 Figure 6 but near the lower end in v4 Figure A18, with overlapping error bars. v4 also adds Table A9 results and reports performance saturation at five groups, with a six-percentage-point error increase using two. Existing SOP and baseline values in Table 1 and matched fidelity, insertion/deletion, and probing tables remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The insertion/deletion definitions, lower-bound results, zero-error group constructions, conjectures, and proofs are retained in Section 2 and Appendix A. Renumbering, group-symbol standardization, and repaired cross-references do not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and four introduction contributions retain the same claims about learnable groups, theoretical limitations of per-feature SANNs, competitive performance, and debugging/cosmology utility. The shortened conclusion preserves this contribution scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 qualifies cosmological weights as conditional on structures being used, removes speculation about other signals driving sigma8, and frames discovery as a promising step. Figure A18 emphasizes similar human-evaluation scores across methods, although Appendix C.4.6 retains the older claim that SOP is among the most distinctive.

D1.justification: v4 specifies CosmoGrid's 66-by-66 inputs, two outputs, and 14-by-14-by-32 hidden states, while removing watershed/scikit-image instructions. Appendix C.2.2 newly identifies a half-epoch ImageNet checkpoint within the retained one-epoch training budget. Hardware, code access, and the controllable-baseline 20-pass budget were already disclosed in v3.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations for FastSHAP, ViT-Shapley, AutoGnothi, and Yang et al.'s 2024 concept-based work, and removes the Beucher and Grady segmentation references. The broader positioning against existing SANNs and attribution theory remains stable.

P1.justification: v4 restructures dataset descriptions into lists, shortens the conclusion, standardizes terminology and notation, and edits acknowledgments. Algorithm 1 moves into the main text and the human distinction discussion moves into the appendix; most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a two-column conference layout for the main text and extensively resizes and rearranges displays. Fidelity tables merge into Table A5, other insertion/deletion tables merge into A6-A7, and ImageNet insertion/deletion moves into the main text. New displays include the computation-cost table, additional-baseline table, and deletion curves in Figure A16.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens evaluation by addressing v3's very small human-study sample, adding relevant Shapley-approximation comparisons, and examining the performance/computation tradeoff through group-count controls. Its cosmology interpretation is also more carefully qualified. These gains are limited by inconsistent human-study prose: Appendix C.4.6 still calls SOP highly distinctive despite its low mean ranking in the revised Figure A18.
